messages:
maya (pm): Quick sync: we need to decide prioritization + sequencing for the flex-commit pricing idea vs pushing reserved-only for enterprise customers. Customers are asking for: predictable costs, burstability, and simple SLAs. Thoughts?

sam (eng): From infra side: reserved capacity is easiest to guarantee SLOs & latency. Flex commits add a scheduling/overprovisioning layer and more complexity (autoscale policies + accounting).

li (infra): Agree. Also caching/burst routing becomes trickier if we need to guarantee reserved latency for commit customers while still supporting PAYG bursts.

toni (sales): Customers love the idea of a commit where they can bank credits but want the ability to burst for holiday spikes. They'd trade some discount for burst credits.

jay (growth): For self-serve growth motion, tiers + generous free burst is better. Flex commits sound enterprise-y; could confuse signups.

maya (pm): Let's try a quick RICE-style sketch to compare:
- Reach: enterprise-only commit pilots ~10 accounts (low), tiering changes impact all new signups (high)
- Impact: commits -> big ARR predictability (high), tier tweak -> better conversion (med)
- Confidence: infra cost for commit unknown (low), tier change low risk (high)
- Effort: commit infra + billing changes (high), tier UI + docs (low)

sam (eng): RICE makes me nervous because effort/unknowns for commit are bigger than it looks. If we greenlight commit we need a scoped MVP:
1) Simple accounting: a monthly credit bucket that depletes per-token.
2) Burst policy: allow short-term bursts to PAYG at higher rate when bucket exhausted.
3) Dedicated SLA flag for requests routed to reserved pool.

li (infra): Implementation note: minimal viable reserved routing could be an API header x-scope:reserved and a routing rule. Billing side needs reconciliation job. Example config:
```
reserved_pool:{
  capacity: 100k_tokens_per_min,
  burst_window: 60s,
  burst_rate: 2x
}
```
That's doable as a pilot.

toni (sales): Can we offer a 6-month pilot with a small discount and burst credits? We can commit to 3 customers to start.

maya (pm): Sequencing proposal:
- Phase 1 (4 wks): Tier + burst messaging (low effort) + evaluate analytics impact.
- Phase 2 (6-8 wks): Internal pilot infra + billing PoC for 3 enterprise customers.
- Phase 3 (Q3): Full flex-commit productization if pilot validates economics and SLOs.

jay (growth): +1 for doing tier changes first. Gives us data to refine pricing elasticity before committing big infra work.

sam (eng): Action items for infra: sketch routing + billing PoC, identify rollback plan if reserved routing causes latency regressions. ETA 2 weeks for design doc.

li (infra): I'll add perf guardrails: circuit-breaker when reserved pool latency >200ms -> fallback to PAYG routing. Need metrics and alerts.

toni (sales): I'll shortlist 3 potential pilot accounts this week and ping them about a 6-month pilot with burst credits.

maya (pm): Decision: Do tier changes first (low effort), run pilot for flex-commit reserved in parallel design. If pilot shows >=10% net margin improvement for those customers, we escalate to productization.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: created issue #PR-452: "Flex-commit pilot: routing + billing PoC" assigned to sam, due 2026-04-08

maya (pm): Thanks team — will capture this in the roadmap doc and add acceptance criteria:
- pilot customers onboarded
- end-to-end billing reconciliation passes
- perf SLOs met for reserved flag 95th p90 latency thresholds
- pricing elasticity signals from tier change

jay (growth): I'll track conversion delta from tier change and send a summary in two weeks.

sam (eng): Filing design doc link: https://redwood.internal/notes/flex-commit-design (WIP)

maya (pm): Closing thread — followups in roadmap PR and the infra issue. :rocket:
